chapter: Back in New York: Heard and Dizzy
title: Joining J.C. Heard's band at Cafe Society
summary: On a break from Claude Hopkins he sat in at Cafe Society, replaced Budd Johnson with J.C. Heard, and wrote his first chart, Who's Sorry Now.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: O.K. Getting back for a minute to the sequence of bands you were in. You mentioned Claude Hopkins and your time with him. Now, when you left Claude Hopkins, who did you go with after that?

What happened...you know after the show you had about an hour and a half break and so I went down to Cafe Society. I took a cab and went down there, because Sarah Vaughan was workin' there and J.C. Heard band was there and he had George Treadwell was in the band and Dicky Harris and Jimmy Jones was playin' piano and I loved him so and, of course, J.C. Heard and Al McKibbon. So I went down and J.C. asked me to play one because Budd Johnson had quit the band. And I played "How Deep is the Ocean" and they liked it and so...and then Sarah Vaughan was there and she give me encouragement, she say "That sound so good." And that knocked me out. So then I went back up there (Zanzibar) and didn't say nothin' to nobody. Then I went on down with J.C. Heard. And that was really a fine job, 'cause J.C. Heard is so marvelous and he was so clean, you know. We rehearsed and Jimmy was writing things and that's when I started writing some things. I think my first music for the band was "Who's Sorry Now". And we were broadcasting three nights a week, I mean three times a night.
